scope: Source-level mathematical analysis and executed current-compiler boundary probes. This is neither an imported GLEAN proof nor a claim that an abstract graph proves π irrational. Original-source verification is independently recorded by the reference runner.
mainConclusion: Current GLEAN cannot yet start this genuine proof in its formal model: the target itself is outside its grammar. The bottleneck is mathematical representation and project/Lean integration, before canvas styling. Preserve the existing useful node UX while adding Lean-backed typed, scoped components and source-backed opaque blocks.

mathOutline.claim: Define I n θ = ∫[-1,1] (1-x²)^n cos(xθ) dx and derive a recurrence by integration by parts.
Construct integer-coefficient sinPoly/cosPoly recursively; bound the degree of sinPoly n by n; express I n θ·θ^(2n+1) through n! and their sine/cosine combination.
Prove integer polynomial evaluation at a/b becomes integral after multiplying by b^k when degree ≤ k.
Under a rationality contradiction assumption obtain π/2=a/b, b>0 and a>0; select n for which t=a^(2n+1)/n!·I n(π/2) satisfies 0<t<1.
Use the degree bound and polynomial identity to equate t with an integer z, giving 0<z<1; cast to ℤ and derive a contradiction.

dependencyCaveat: Dependencies listed here are manually read local source references, including names in types and definitions; they are not an extracted kernel dependency graph. Recursive self references indicate structural recursion, never unguarded graph cycles. cosPoly_natDegree_le is not in the main theorem source-level dependency closure.
privateNameImplication: The public theorem is globally named irrational_pi (not Real.irrational_pi). All 15 local declarations are private. A component palette importing this module cannot simply reference the short names I, sinPoly, is_integer, etc.; in-file source context/private declaration identity must be retained rather than exporting them as public APIs.
